problem: State-of-the-art visual navigation policies such as NoMaD and GNM are supervised and 'hard-coded' once trained. New constraints (e.g. 'no left turns') cannot be added at test time, and extra compute cannot be spent on hard cases. Prior diffusion world models (DIAMOND, GameNGen) each model a single game or environment rather than many real-world environments and embodiments.
motivation: Humans plan by imagining future trajectories under constraints and counterfactuals. A controllable video world model that predicts egocentric observations from actions would let an agent simulate candidate plans and check whether they reach a goal. Pooling heterogeneous robot navigation video, plus action-free egocentric video, makes it possible to train one large diffusion transformer that scales with model size and data across embodiments.
key_idea: Train a 1B-parameter Conditional Diffusion Transformer (CDiT) on multi-robot egocentric video to predict future latent frames from past frames, a navigation action (translation + yaw) and a time shift, then plan by simulating candidate trajectories with CEM (or ranking NoMaD samples) and scoring the final imagined frame's LPIPS similarity to the goal image.
insight: Restricting self-attention to the target frame and reading past frames only through cross-attention makes cost linear in context length. In Fig. 5, CDiT-L beats DiT-XL at about 4x fewer FLOPs, and CDiT scales well up to 1B parameters. Table 1 shows three training choices matter. Sampling 4 goals per state to create natural counterfactuals improves 4s prediction on RECON (LPIPS 0.312→0.296). Longer context helps (1 frame 0.304 → 4 frames 0.296). Time-only conditioning collapses (LPIPS 0.760), while action+time is best (0.295). An imagine-and-score planner can beat hard-coded policies: standalone CEM planning gets ATE 1.13 vs NoMaD 1.93 on RECON. The gain is not uniform, though; on HuRoN NWM-only (ATE 4.12) is worse than GNM/NoMaD. Action-free Ego4D video improves prediction in an unseen environment (Go Stanford) but hurts most in-domain datasets (RECON LPIPS 0.295→0.368).
method: Formulation: world model F maps m=4 past SD-VAE latents plus action a=(u∈R², yaw ϕ, time shift k) to the next latent. Actions come from robot odometry deltas summed over k steps (Eq. 2), with k up to ±16 s; per-agent step sizes are normalized and backward motion is filtered out.

CDiT block: self-attention only over tokens of the frame being denoised, then cross-attention from those target tokens to past-frame tokens, then an MLP. This gives O(mn²d) instead of DiT's O(m²n²d). Action, time-shift and diffusion-timestep embeddings (sine-cosine + 2-layer MLP, summed into ξ) modulate the block via AdaLN.

Diffusion training: DiT noise schedule and hyperparameters, simple MSE loss plus a VLB covariance loss. There are 4 random goals per context (batch 1024×4 = 4096), CDiT-XL has 1B parameters, and training uses AdamW at lr 8e-5 on 64 H100s. For unlabeled Ego4D video the action term is simply omitted from ξ.

Standalone planning (MPC via Cross-Entropy Method): the energy is −similarity(decoded final frame, goal) plus large penalties for invalid actions or unsafe states. The trajectory is parametrized as a straight line with endpoint (Δx, Δy, ϕ), split into 8 steps with k=0.25 s. CEM draws N=120 candidates, rolls each out 3 times and scores by mean LPIPS, running a single iteration with per-dataset initial mean/variance.

Constrained planning: action constraints ('forward first', 'left-right first', 'straight then forward') are enforced by zeroing action components for certain steps, and CEM optimizes the remaining steps.

Ranking an external policy: sample 16 or 32 length-8 trajectories from NoMaD, roll each out autoregressively in NWM, and pick the one whose final predicted frame has the lowest LPIPS to the goal image.

Efficiency and adaptation: Time Skip composes adjacent actions to simulate 8 instead of 16 states, and distillation cuts denoising steps from 250 to 6. Together these bring a single 4s rollout from 30.3 s to 0.4 s on an RTX 6000 Ada. Optional test-time adaptation fine-tunes for 2k steps on unknown-environment trajectories.

setting.backbone: CDiT-XL (1B-param Conditional Diffusion Transformer, trained from scratch) on frozen Stable Diffusion VAE latents; LPIPS as goal-scoring function; optionally NoMaD as proposal policy for ranking
setting.training_data: Robot navigation video with odometry-derived actions: SCAND (484 train segments), TartanDrive (1,000), RECON (9,468), HuRoN (2,451). The generalization variant adds 1,619 unlabeled Ego4D videos (~908 h, navigation-like scenarios) using time shift as the only action. GO Stanford is used only for evaluation.
setting.observation: egocentric monocular RGB (4 context frames, 224x224 via SD-VAE latents) + goal image
setting.action_space: continuous relative actions: 2D translation (forward/lateral) + yaw + time shift k; plans are 8-step trajectories at k=0.25 s (≈2 s horizon)
setting.simulator: none — offline evaluation on recorded real-world robot datasets (RECON, HuRoN, SCAND, TartanDrive, GO Stanford)
setting.privileged: goal image of the target location; evaluation is open-loop against ground-truth trajectories. CEM initialization mean/variance for Δx is hand-set per dataset (e.g. (−0.1, 0.02) for RECON).

numbers_note: No standard embodied-navigation benchmark is used (no SR/SPL). All navigation results are offline, open-loop trajectory-prediction errors (ATE/RPE) on recorded robot datasets. Table 7's header says 'RTE' but the caption says RPE, so the key used here is RPE. RECON ranking rows differ between Table 2 (×16: 1.83/0.50, ×32: 1.78/0.48) and Table 7 (×16: 1.88/0.51, ×32: 1.79/0.49); NoMaD also differs (1.93 vs 1.95). Table 2 values are reported above. CDiT-vs-DiT scaling (Fig. 5) and FID/LPIPS vs. horizon against DIAMOND (Fig. 4) are given only as plots. Additional LPIPS (Table 5): SCAND 0.403, TartanDrive 0.414 in-domain; +Ego4D gives RECON 0.368, HuRoN 0.377, SCAND 0.398, TartanDrive 0.430. Additional FVD (Table 6): TartanDrive 494.247, SCAND 401.699. Constraint-planning results (Table 3) are deltas relative to unconstrained planning.
results: Standalone CEM planning with NWM reaches ATE 1.13 / RPE 0.35 on RECON, against NoMaD 1.93/0.52 and GNM 1.87/0.73. It also wins on SCAND (1.28/0.33 vs NoMaD 2.24/0.49) and TartanDrive (5.63/1.18), but on HuRoN its ATE (4.12) is worse than GNM (3.71) and NoMaD (3.73). Ranking 32 NoMaD samples with NWM consistently improves NoMaD, e.g. RECON 1.78/0.48. As a video model NWM far outperforms DIAMOND (16 s FVD on RECON 200.969 vs 762.734). Adding unlabeled Ego4D improves unseen-environment prediction (Go Stanford LPIPS 0.658→0.652) at a cost in-domain.
limitations: Out of distribution, rollouts slowly lose context and drift toward training-like frames (mode collapse). The model also struggles to simulate dynamic agents such as pedestrians.

Evaluation is offline and open-loop on recorded datasets with short (~2 s) horizons. There is no closed-loop or real-robot deployment and no standard embodied benchmark. Standalone planning assumes straight-line trajectories, uses a single CEM iteration, and relies on hand-set per-dataset initialization.
Inference is expensive (30.3 s per 4 s trajectory rollout without Time Skip and distillation; 120×3 rollouts per CEM plan). Actions are limited to 3-DoF planar motion.
